long_biography.plain_text:
At electrical distributor Rexel, Roberto Quarta supported a return to the stock market as a way to reduce debt and fund further growth. As supervisory board chairman, he explained that access to public capital would give the business greater flexibility. The transition also brought separate management and supervisory boards, with committees covering strategy, audit, pay and appointments.

When his private-equity firm pursued engineering-services group SPIE, Quarta pointed to experience at Rexel as a source of knowledge about its markets. The proposed acquisition paired the investors with SPIE’s existing managers and included wider employee share ownership. He emphasised the company’s resilience and opportunities for expansion in France and Europe.
